# 2 Kings Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 237v–239r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_017_page_473.jpg, 2KI_017_page_474.jpg, 2KI_017_page_475.jpg, 2KI_017_page_476.jpg

---

**17:1** In-the-twelfth year of-Achaz king of-Yehudah, became-king [malakh] Hoshea son of-Elah in-Shomron over Yisra'el, nine years.

**17:2** And-he-did the-evil [ha-ra'] in-the-eyes of-YHWH, only [raq] not as-the-kings of-Yisra'el who were before-him.

**17:3** Against-him came-up [alah] Shalmaneser king of-Ashur, and-became Hoshea a-servant [eved] to-him and-returned [vayashev] to-him tribute [minchah].

**17:4** And-found [vayimtsa] the-king of-Ashur in-Hoshea a-conspiracy [qesher], for he-had-sent messengers [mal'akhim] to-So king of-Mitsrayim, and-did-not bring-up [he'elah] tribute to-the-king of-Ashur as-year by-year [ke-shanah be-shanah]. And-seized-him [vaya'atseruhu] the-king of-Ashur and-bound-him [vaya'asrehu] in-the-house of-confinement [bet kele'].

**17:5** And-went-up the-king of-Ashur in-all the-land, and-went-up to-Shomron and-besieged [vayatsar] upon-it three years.

**17:6** In-the-ninth year of-Hoshea, the-king of-Ashur captured [lakhad] Shomron and-exiled [vayegel] Yisra'el to-Ashur, and-settled-them [vayoshev] in-Chalach and-in-Chavor [by] the-river [nehar] Gozan and-[in] the-cities of-Maday.

**17:7** And-it-was [vayehi] because [ki] the-sons of-Yisra'el had-sinned [chat'u] against-YHWH their-God, the-one-bringing-them-up [ha-ma'aleh otam] from-the-land of-Mitsrayim, from-under the-hand of-Par'oh king of-Mitsrayim, and-they-feared [vayir'u] other gods ['elohim acherim].

**17:8** And-they-walked in-the-statutes [be-chuqqot] of-the-nations whom YHWH had-dispossessed [horish] from-before the-sons of-Yisra'el, and-[the statutes] of-the-kings of-Yisra'el that they-made ['asu].

**17:9** And-covered [vayechappu] the-sons of-Yisra'el words [devarim] that [were] not-right [lo khen] against-YHWH their-God, and-built for-themselves high-places [bamot] in-all their-cities, from-tower of-watchmen [migdal notsrim] to-fortified city [ir mibtsar].

**17:10** And-they-set-up for-themselves pillars [matstsevot] and-Asherim [asherim] upon every high hill [giv'ah gevohah] and-under every green [ra'anan] tree.

**17:11** And-they-burned-incense [vayeqatteru] there in-all the-high-places, like-the-nations whom YHWH had-exiled [heglah] from-before-them, and-they-did evil [ra'ot] things to-provoke [le-hakh'is] YHWH.

**17:12** And-they-served the-idols [ha-gillulim] of-which YHWH had-said to-them: You-shall-not do this thing [ha-davar ha-zeh].

**17:13** And-warned [vaya'ad] YHWH against-Yisra'el and-against-Yehudah by-the-hand of-every prophet [navi], every seer [chozeh], saying: Turn [shuvu] from your-evil ways [darkheykhem ha-ra'im] and-keep my-commandments [mitsvotay], my-statutes [chuqqotay], according-to-all the-Torah [ha-torah] that I-commanded your-fathers and-that I-sent to-you by-the-hand of-my-servants the-prophets [avadai ha-nevi'im].

**17:14** And-they-did-not listen [lo sham'u] and-hardened [vayaqshu] their-neck [orpam] like-the-neck of-their-fathers who did-not believe [lo he'eminu] in-YHWH their-God.

**17:15** And-they-rejected [vayim'asu] his-statutes [chuqqotav] and-his-covenant [berito] that he-cut [karat] with their-fathers, and-his-testimonies [edotav] that he-testified [he'id] against-them, and-they-went after the-vanity [ha-hevel] and-became-vain [vayehbalu], and-after the-nations that [were] around-them, of-which YHWH had-commanded them not-to-do like-them.

**17:16** And-they-forsook ['azvu] all the-commandments [mitsvot] of-YHWH their-God, and-made for-themselves a-molten-image [massekah], two calves ['agalim], and-made an-Asherah [asherah], and-bowed-down [vayishtachavu] to-all the-host [tseva] of-the-heavens [ha-shamayim], and-served Ba'al.

**17:17** And-they-passed [vaya'aviru] their-sons and-their-daughters through-the-fire, and-practiced-divination [vayiqsemu qesamim] and-practiced-sorcery [vayenachashu], and-sold-themselves [vayitmakreru] to-do the-evil in-the-eyes of-YHWH, to-provoke-him [le-hakh'iso].

**17:18** And-was-very-angry [vayit'annaph] YHWH greatly [me'od] with-Yisra'el, and-removed-them [vayesirem] from-upon his-face [panav]. None [lo] remained [nish'ar] except [raq] the-tribe [shevet] of-Yehudah alone [levaddo].

**17:19** Also [gam] Yehudah did-not keep [lo shamar] the-commandments of-YHWH their-God, and-they-walked in-the-statutes of-Yisra'el that they-had-made.

**17:20** And-rejected [vayim'as] YHWH all the-seed [zerah] of-Yisra'el, and-afflicted-them [vaye'annem] and-gave-them [vayittenem] into-the-hand of-plunderers [shosim], until he-cast-them [hishlikham] from-upon his-face.

**17:21** For he-tore [qara'] Yisra'el from-upon the-house of-David, and-they-made-king [vayamlikhu] Yerov'am son of-Nevat. And-drove [vayaddach] Yerov'am Yisra'el from-after YHWH and-caused-them-to-sin [hecheti'am] a-great sin [chata'ah gedolah].

**17:22** And-walked the-sons of-Yisra'el in-all the-sins [chattot] of-Yerov'am that he-did; they-did-not depart [lo saru] from-them,

**17:23** until YHWH removed [hesir] Yisra'el from-upon his-face, as he-had-spoken [dibber] by-the-hand of-all his-servants the-prophets. And-was-exiled [vayigel] Yisra'el from-upon its-land ['admato] to-Ashur, to this day [ad ha-yom ha-zeh].

**17:24** And-brought [vayave'] the-king of-Ashur from-Bavel and-from-Kutah and-from-Avva and-from-Chamat and-Sepharvaim, and-settled [vayoshev] [them] in-the-cities of-Shomron in-place-of [tachat] the-sons of-Yisra'el. And-they-possessed [vayirshu] Shomron and-dwelt in-its-cities.

**17:25** And-it-was at-the-beginning of-their-dwelling there, they-did-not fear [lo yare'u] YHWH, and-sent [vayeshalach] YHWH among-them the-lions [ha-arayot], and-they-were killing [mehamitim] among-them.

**17:26** And-they-said to-the-king of-Ashur, saying: The-nations that you-exiled and-settled in-the-cities of-Shomron do-not know [lo yade'u] the-custom [mishpat] of-the-god of-the-land ['elohey ha-arets], and-he-has-sent among-them the-lions, and-behold, they-are-killing them, because they-do-not know the-custom of-the-god of-the-land.

**17:27** And-commanded the-king of-Ashur, saying: Send [holikhu] there one of-the-priests whom you-exiled from-there, and-let-them-go and-dwell there, and-let-him-teach-them [veyorem] the-custom of-the-god of-the-land.

**17:28** And-came one of-the-priests whom they-had-exiled from-Shomron, and-dwelt in-Beit-El, and-he-was teaching-them [moreh otam] how they-should-fear [yir'u] YHWH.

**17:29** And-were making [oyim], each nation [goy goy], its-gods ['elohav], and-placed [them] in-the-houses of-the-high-places [batey ha-bamot] that the-Shomronim had-made, each nation in-their-cities where they [were] dwelling.

**17:30** And-the-men of-Bavel made Sukkot-Benot, and-the-men of-Kut made Nergal, and-the-men of-Chamat made Ashima,

**17:31** and-the-Avvim made Nivchaz and-Tartak, and-the-Sepharvim were-burning [sorfim] their-sons in-the-fire to-Adrammelekh and-Anammelekh, gods ['elohey] of-Sepharvaim.

**17:32** And-they-were fearing [yere'im] YHWH, and-made for-themselves from-their-extremities [miqtsotam] priests of-high-places [kohaney bamot], and-they-were acting [osim] for-them in-the-houses of-the-high-places.

**17:33** YHWH they-were fearing [yere'im], and-their-own gods they-were serving ['ovdim], according-to-the-custom of-the-nations from-which they-had-been-exiled [higlu otam] from-there.

**17:34** To this day they-are doing [osim] according-to-the-former customs [ka-mishpatim ha-rishonim]. They-do-not fear [yere'im] YHWH, and-they-do-not do according-to-their-statutes and-according-to-their-customs, and-according-to-the-Torah and-according-to-the-commandment that YHWH commanded the-sons of-Ya'aqov whom he-named [sam shemo] Yisra'el.

**17:35** And-had-cut [vayikhrot] YHWH with-them a-covenant [berit] and-had-commanded-them, saying: You-shall-not fear other gods, and-you-shall-not bow-down to-them and-you-shall-not serve-them and-you-shall-not sacrifice to-them.

**17:36** But YHWH, who-brought-you-up from-the-land of-Mitsrayim with-great power [be-koach gadol] and-with-an-outstretched arm [u-vizroa netuyah] — him you-shall-fear [oto tira'u] and-to-him you-shall-bow-down and-to-him you-shall-sacrifice.

**17:37** And-the-statutes and-the-ordinances [ha-mishpatim] and-the-Torah and-the-commandment that he-wrote for-you, you-shall-observe [tishmeru] to-do [la'asot] all the-days, and-you-shall-not fear other gods.

**17:38** And-the-covenant that I-cut with-you, you-shall-not forget [lo tishkachu], and-you-shall-not fear other gods.

**17:39** But YHWH your-God you-shall-fear, and-he will-deliver-you [yatsil etkhem] from-the-hand of-all your-enemies ['oyveykhem].

**17:40** And-they-did-not listen [lo sham'u], but according-to-their-former custom [ke-mishpatam ha-rishon] they-were doing [osim].

**17:41** And-these nations were fearing [yere'im] YHWH and-their-carved-images [pesileihem] they-were serving ['ovdim]. Also [gam] their-sons and-their-sons' sons — as their-fathers did, they are-doing to this day.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.6 — Deportation sites:** Halah, Habor (on the river Gozan), and the cities of the Medes represent the far corners of the Assyrian empire. The precision of the locations underscores the finality of exile — Israel is scattered to the empire's periphery.

**v.9 — *vayechappu*:** "They covered" — literally, the Israelites "covered over" or "concealed" things against YHWH. The exact meaning is debated; it may mean they attributed false qualities to YHWH, or secretly practiced forbidden things. The LXX differs significantly here.

**v.15 — *ha-hevel vayehbalu*:** "The vanity and they became vain" — a cognate accusative construction. Israel pursued emptiness and became empty. The verb derives from the noun — you become what you worship. This is the narrator's core theological insight, echoing Jeremiah 2:5.

**v.23 — "to this day":** This phrase reveals the narrator's temporal standpoint — writing after 722 BCE, looking back at a permanent exile. The northern kingdom will never return. This is the narrator's obituary for Israel.

**v.33 — The paradox:** "YHWH they were fearing, and their own gods they were serving." The narrator presents this as a theological impossibility — you cannot both fear YHWH and serve other gods. The Samaritans' religion is presented as fundamentally contradictory.

**v.34 — Ambiguity of referent:** "They do not fear YHWH" — it is debated whether "they" refers to the foreign settlers (whose YHWH-worship is inadequate) or the original Israelites (whose covenant-breaking is the root cause). The narrator may deliberately allow both readings.

*— EMET*
